text: Reading Alan Watts and some philosophy helped me put it in context. Talking to my parents. Time.

After the incident I finally got into the VA system properly. My lawyer helped push that. I was assigned a psychiatrist and a therapist. The first therapist did prolonged exposure therapy, which was brutal, especially at the beginning, but it did help with the nightmares. I was put on prazosin for nightmares, which helped a lot, and sertraline, which I'm not sure did much. I tried several other medications for sleep that made me groggy and I stopped them.

I went to an inpatient program for veterans with PTSD and substance use for eight weeks. That was the turning point. Being around other guys who understood, getting sober, having structure. I've been sober for 14 months now.

My wife and I did couples counselling, which helped her understand what was going on and helped me move back into our bedroom. I've been slowly rebuilding my relationship with my kids. My daughter and I do Saturday mornings at the park now, just the two of us.

I joined a peer support group for veterans that meets weekly. That has been very important. I also go fishing with a couple of buddies from the group.

Harmful: the underground session itself, obviously. Also, early on, a VA doctor who basically told me I'd brought it on myself by taking illegal drugs. That made me want to give up on the whole system.

I'm still on the waiting list for the official MDMA trial. I'm not sure if I'll do it. I'm much better than I was, but the flashbacks still come, and I still sleep in a separate room some nights when it's bad.
Clonazepam helped at first, now I mostly just ignore the visuals.

Ich war bei der psychologischen Beratungsstelle der Uni, die mir sehr geholfen haben, die Erfahrung einzuordnen. Außerdem habe ich angefangen, regelmäßig Sport zu machen, vor allem Klettern, das bringt mich in meinen Körper. Ich habe viel über Philosophie gelesen, das hat mir geholfen, die Gedanken zu ordnen. Und die Zeit hat geholfen. Ich nehme keine Psychedelika mehr.
Time, and talking to friends who weren't part of the group.

Ich habe mit einem Coach über meine Ängste im Job gesprochen, das hat etwas geholfen. Mit meiner Partnerin habe ich viel darüber geredet. Am Ende habe ich den Job gewechselt, weil ich mich in dem Team nicht mehr wohlgefühlt habe. Im neuen Job ist es besser, aber die Angst in Meetings ist noch nicht ganz weg.

I saw a few different therapists. The first one didn't understand anything about psychedelics and just said it was anxiety. The second one was better, she had some experience with DP/DR and helped me with grounding and with not 'checking' reality all the time.

I was put on an SSRI and later an SNRI, neither helped the derealisation, though maybe a little with the depression. I stopped them after a year.

Reading philosophy helped surprisingly, especially about how other philosophers dealt with solipsism and why it's not a useful position. Talking to people at a psychedelic integration circle helped a lot because I met others who'd had similar 'simulation' experiences and came out the other side.

Going outside, running, cooking, anything physical and sensory helps. Screens make it worse, especially video games, which I've mostly given up.

Unhelpful: Reddit forums where people talked about DP/DR as permanent and incurable. I spent hours on those and they made me feel hopeless.
I talked to a counsellor a few times, which helped me process the fear. I think about it differently now, more as a lesson. I drink a lot more water now lol.

Ich mache seit über einem Jahr eine Psychotherapie und nehme Antidepressiva. Beides hilft ein wenig, aber ich bin noch lange nicht da, wo ich vorher war. Ich gehe zu einer Selbsthilfegruppe für Menschen mit Depressionen, das hilft mir, mich weniger allein zu fühlen. Am schwierigsten ist, dass meine Familie nicht versteht, warum ich nicht einfach wieder 'normal' werde. Ich habe immer noch Tage, an denen ich nicht aufstehen kann.
Ich habe eine Psychotherapie begonnen, die mir hilft, die Erinnerungen an meine Kindheit zu verarbeiten. Ich spreche mehr mit meinem Partner darüber, was in mir vorgeht. Es wird langsam besser.
